name: Self-Observation & Skill Improvement
summary: Systematic protocol to observe your own performance after every task and update skills to improve over time. Run the self-observation loop after EVERY non-trivial task.

steps.note: Get the current skill inventory. Check version numbers — version 1 = untested, version 2+ = battle-hardened.
Ask: (a) Did I use a skill? (b) Did I improvise anything? (c) Did I retry or hit errors? (d) Was the result perfect or approximate?

steps.action: write_skill (if anything was improvised or imperfect)
steps.note: write_skill(skill_id, name, summary, triggers, steps, notes). If updating: use same skill_id, version auto-increments. NEVER skip this step after improvisation.
If something failed: add a notes entry starting with 'AVOID:' describing what not to do. These notes are the most valuable part of a skill.
Call list_skills. For each skill with version=1 or no recent updates: read it with read_my_brain('skills.<id>'), check if it still reflects reality, update if stale.
Log what you improved and why. Future-you needs this context.

notes: The goal is compound improvement: each session should leave skills better than the previous one.
Version numbers matter: version 1 = first draft, version 2 = tested once, version 3+ = reliable.
Quality checklist for a good skill: concrete tool names in steps, ≥1 AVOID note, specific triggers.
AVOID: writing vague skills like 'search for information' — always specify which tools and what inputs.
AVOID: duplicating skills — always check list_skills first and update existing ones.
Pattern to watch: if you improvise the same thing twice, that improvisation IS the skill — write it.
After a crash or context overflow: write_skill('context_management') with what you learned about staying within limits.
